title: cost-optimization: autotune batching/caching defaults + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Priya Shah
description: Motivation: Reduce per-token unit cost for common production workloads by automatically recommending and applying batching/caching defaults, surfaced quantization profiles, and unit-economics tooling. Scope: runtime defaults for batching and prefix/KV caching, on-device quantization profile registry + selection heuristics, and a small CLI + console surface for unit-econ analysis. Changes are designed to be opt-in via config flags and gated by safety checks. Checklist: - [x] implement batching default heuristics and config layer - [x] add prefix/KV cache tuning and safe fallbacks - [x] implement quantization profile registry and selection heuristics - [x] add CLI and console tooling to compute unit economics per model/route - [x] unit and integration tests - [x] docs and migration notes - [x] smoke tests on staging Key decisions: default batching is now workload-aware (seq-len histogram + p95 latency SLO) rather than static token-window; prefix/KV cache default TTL is conservative and only enabled for routes with privacy-safe markers; quantization profiles are stored as YAML artifacts in the model registry and recommended by heuristics that consider model arch + target latency/quality budget. Rollout plan: staged canary in dedicated region 'eu-west-1' for 2 weeks, followed by gradual global rollout with opt-out via route config. Backwards compatibility: defaults are additive and off unless tenant opt-in; the CLI can simulate cost impact without changing runtime. Related: ENG-3121 improves batching heuristics; SUP-7421 incident analysis influenced the conservative TTL decision. Testing: unit tests for heuristics, end-to-end load tests with synthetic workloads, manual QA on console. Impact: expected 8-14% median unit-cost reduction on mixed text-generation workloads in staging with negligible p99 latency regressions. See release_notes for more detail.

review_comments: Riley Chen: Nice work, Priya. A few questions about the heuristics: how do you avoid oscillation when load patterns change? Priya Shah: We use an exponential backoff on policy changes and require sustained signal over configurable windows; added tests to cover this. Ethan Walker: Please add a migration note for Dedicated customers who pin batching configs. Priya Shah: Added docs/notes and a helm-values override; Dedicated will remain opt-in. Alicia Gomez: The quant profiles look good; can we add a safety check if a profile causes quality regressions in canary? Priya Shah: Implemented a binary safety gate in the rollout manifest that runs evals against a small prompt set prior to enabling a profile; documented behavior. CI flakiness: initial CI run failed on a flaky integration test (tests/integration/test_autotune_end2end.py) due to an env race; fixed by adding a service readiness check and re-run. Final review: Approved by Ethan Walker and Riley Chen. Merge: squash and merge once CI is green.
release_notes: Automatic cost-optimization automation: adds workload-aware batching defaults, conservative prefix/KV caching defaults, quantization profile registry and selection heuristics, and a unit-economics CLI + console surface. Rollout is gated and opt-in for tenants. Expected median unit-cost reductions of 8-14% for mixed generation workloads. See docs/notes/cost-optimization-automation.md for migration steps.
